Definition: from G182; instability, i.e. disorder:--commotion, confusion, tumult.
BiblicalUsage: The word is instability, disorder, tumult. Jesus warns of commotions before the end; Paul says God is not the author of confusion, but of peace; he fears finding strifes, envyings, wraths, tumults in Corinth; and James says where envying and strife are, there is confusion and every evil work. In every case the word marks what God is not the author of.
TheologicalSignificance: Confusion is the fingerprint of the wrong spirit. I believe the test is simple and Paul gives it: God is the author of peace, so where there is settled disorder and strife, look for envy and selfish ambition behind it — and deal with those first.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Paul; James, Brother of Jesus
